title: Alex Hormozi on focus, elite talent, brand and skills: the shifts behind $40M to $100M+
summary: Alex explains three shifts behind Acquisition.com's growth: ruthless single-objective focus, paying for elite talent, and betting on brand with delayed payoff. He also argues for investing in your own skills over stocks, treating volatility as a volume problem, and turning vague traits into concrete behaviors.

principles.text: Focus from the top down: pick one objective, finish it, then move to the next. Sequencing beats parallel work.
principles.quote: you actually get 5 things done faster when you do them in order than trying to do all 5 at once.

principles.text: Pay for elite talent. The best people return 100x, so a high salary is still the cheaper option.
principles.quote: it's worth paying someone 1,000,000 of dollars a year if they can make you tens of 1,000,000 or 100 of 1,000,000 of dollars a year.

principles.text: Brand pays off on a delay, so start planting now and keep investing even when results lag.
principles.quote: you wanna dig the well before you're thirsty.

principles.text: Early on, invest in your own skills rather than the stock market. Active income beats passive returns at small scale.
principles.quote: don't invest in the S and P 500. It's invest in the S and Me 500.

principles.text: Inconsistent results usually mean too little volume. Raise the number of attempts before you judge the method.
principles.quote: most volatility comes from lack of volume

principles.text: Ask what it would take to reach a goal, then decide whether the price is worth paying.
principles.quote: what would it take? And the reason I love that question is because it assumes success.
